posts.text: This week: two oil chokepoints threatened at once, occupied Lebanese ground changing hands, and a new commander for Europe's longest front line. Five ways the map moved — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ US strikes on Iran hit an 11th straight night, spreading to new provinces. Iran hit back at Bahrain, Kuwait & Jordan, pulling in a 5th country. Pentagon says the war has cost $37.5bn so far. (BBC, Guardian, Al Jazeera, NYT, DW)

2/ Yemen's Houthis declared a Red Sea blockade on Saudi Arabia, threatening tankers at Saudi ports. They sit above Bab el-Mandeb — with Hormuz already contested, two of the world's great oil chokepoints are now in play. (NYT, Guardian)

3/ Lebanon's army moved into a 'pilot zone' as Israeli troops withdrew from occupied ground, rare progress. But Lebanon accuses Israeli troops of firing during the handover, and a former US official doubts full withdrawal follows. (BBC, Al Jazeera, NYT)

4/ Zelensky fired Ukraine's top general, Syrskyi, after nationwide protests over the sacking of a popular defence minister. New commander: Mykhailo Drapatyi. Who runs a 1,000km front line shapes where it ends up on the map. (BBC, Guardian, NYT)

5/ Flash floods tore through Nuristan, Afghanistan, killing 23+ and leaving 100+ missing. Steep Hindu Kush valleys funnel rain into torrents fast — the same remoteness that isolates the province slows every rescue. (Guardian, NYT)

The data behind it: this week's $37.5bn war bill, in context. Our World in Data's map of military spending as % of GDP (2025) — Ukraine's share is so far off the scale it's nearly black. Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)
